name: ink-figure
_note: The house style for post headers. YOJI SHINKAWA DOMINANT with Sabogal as seasoning, not the reverse: the base register is a loose gestural black brush-pen drawing on white paper (confident varying strokes, dry-brush breaks, solid black silhouette masses, splatter), and the alchemical-engraving half survives only in the SUBJECT MATTER and the single oxblood wash. The earlier version had this inverted and the inversion was the defect: it read as hermetic etching plates. The palette is still the site's own :root tokens, so a header belongs to the design system.

paper.role: plain paper ground (the site bone token) — NOT an engraved plate

ink.role: black ink — all linework and mass

accent.role: oxblood red — exactly ONE wash per image

model._note: SDXL rather than a Flux/Qwen-class model: those score higher on prompt-following and realism, but for a LOCKED hand across 58 plates a model with a more consistent native style is the right base, and SDXL carries the deepest ink/engraving-lineage LoRA ecosystem if the hand ever needs training to hold.

composition._ratio: 2.4:1 (1536x640), RESTORED 2026-10-01 after the style was flipped to Yoji-dominant. The square was adopted because a wide 1536x640 frame made SDXL fill the width with a ROW of objects — but that measurement was taken with the PATTERNED, engraving-dominant prompt (style versions 1-4), whose 'one emblem, centred, symmetric' phrasing is exactly what repeats under a wide field. A gestural asymmetric hand has no such prior to tile, so the canvas constraint is re-tested here under style v6 rather than assumed to still hold. See _icon_note.
rules: ONE strong mass or figure, but placed ASYMMETRICALLY and often cropped by the frame edge — never a centred, isolated, symmetrical icon
no concentric ornament, no radial symmetry, no decorative border of repeated marks
INK IS THE SUBJECT: a few large confident strokes, not thousands of fine ones
must survive at 240px wide — silhouette first, detail second
composition.seed: derived per slug: first 8 hex digits of sha256(slug) as int, so a slug always renders the same frame
composition._presentation: full-bleed banner in the masthead: the image spans the 732px column at 1536px source (2.1x retina). The wide register is the original layout intent; the centred square plate (480px) was the workaround for the icon/row failure and is retired with it.
composition._icon_note: MEASURED 2026-10-01 (user feedback twice): the batch read as ICONS and as hermetic ETCHINGS. Both are produced by the prompt, not the model. Icons came from the literal words 'emblem' (an icon IS an emblem), 'centred', 'alone in the frame' and 'generous empty paper all around' — a centred isolated symmetrical object on an empty field is the definition of an icon, and 20 of 59 briefs additionally said 'centred in the frame'. Etching came from 'ink drawing on AGED BONE PAPER' plus a clause actually requesting 'fine stippled cross-hatching worked densely into the core'. Removing the engraving texture clause and the aged-paper ground is the fix.

prompt.prefix: a clear ink drawing on white paper,
prompt.style: bold black brush pen strokes, confident varying pressure, thick-to-thin tapering lines, solid black ink masses, strong clear silhouette, high contrast black on white, the object drawn large, deliberately and unmistakably as a recognisable thing, illustrative
prompt.suffix: the object fully inside the picture and clearly readable, off-centre, no ornamental border around the image
prompt.negative: photorealistic, 3d render, glossy, saturated, gradient background, airbrush, smooth vector, digital painting, anime, cartoon, watermark, signature, text, letters, glyphs, runes, numerals, border, frame, plate border, engraving, etching, fine even linework, technical drawing, blueprint, precise mechanical illustration, multiple panels, depth of field, blur, colour photography, sepia photo, vignette edges, cross, crucifix, christian cross, religious symbol, crucifixion, centred, symmetrical, symmetry, mandala, radial symmetry, concentric ornament, crest, badge, logo, ornamental decoration, patterned, tiled, repeated motif, fine stippling, dense hatching, cross-hatching, etching texture, aged paper, stained parchment

seedream._note: The Seedream 5.0 Pro prompt layer. Same house style as the prompt block (Yoji Shinkawa dominant, Sabogal as seasoning) but assembled for a model with NO negative prompt, a ~600-word budget, and a literal reading of a long instruction. The two style clauses lead (hand, then iconography), the SUBSTANCE follows (object, its parts, the composition), and the suppressions close the prompt. It is composed from the brief RAW fields emblem/composition/symbols/accent, never from the SDXL-mangled prompt.
seedream.hand: A loose brush-pen ink drawing on warm white paper, in the concept-art manner of Yoji Shinkawa: bold black ink worked with a brush pen in confident, varying-pressure strokes, lines that taper thick-to-thin, dry-brush breaks where the pen runs dry, the shadow side of every form filled as one solid black mass, and the lit side left as clean untouched paper.
seedream.iconography: The subject carries the hermetic iconography of José Gabriel Alegría Sabogal's reconstructive drawings of magical gems and engraved plates, drawn however with a draftsman's economy rather than a plate's density: a few decisive strokes say everything, and the symbol is a real, nameable object with weight and body, not a flat diagram.
seedream.palette: Black ink on warm white paper throughout, with exactly one wash of deep oxblood red: {accent}. There is no red anywhere else in the image.
seedream.suppress: Every mark in the picture belongs to the drawing itself. The image carries no writing, no lettering, no numerals, no caption and no signature; no border, frame or decorative margin; no ornament arranged symmetrically about a centre; and no photographic, painted, glossy, shaded or three-dimensional rendering. It is only black ink strokes and solid black masses laid on paper.

_negative_note: `text, letters, glyphs, runes` are banned because diffusion models render lettering as convincing nonsense — a header that appears to carry an inscription it does not have is a lie on the page. Where a post needs a real glyph (a planetary sigil, a geometric figure), it is stated in the emblem brief as a SHAPE, or composited by hand afterwards. `engraving, etching, fine even linework, technical drawing` were added after a measured failure: the engraving half of the style is the DEFAULT attractor for this subject matter, so it needs suppressing positively, not just omitting — see ab.py and the note on `order` below.
_order_note: The gestural clause is placed FIRST and the subject text is assembled WITHOUT medium vocabulary, because a 48-word style clause sitting at position 108 of 235 was losing to the subject text around it — the model obeys the most specific, most dominant signal, and the brief's own wording ('dense engraved line', 'engraved like a plate') pulled hard toward engraving. Measured in tools/headers/ab.py: hand-first + engraving stripped turned a purely technical plate into a clearly gestural one at the same seed. The two halves are ordered so the GESTURE sets the medium and the engraving lives only in the core.

subject_vocabulary._note: Per-post emblem briefs draw on this vocabulary. It is deliberately hermetic: the blog's reading series is Proclus, the Chaldean Oracles, Picatrix, Geosophia, Quareia, Set and Setting, black-abbot-white-magic. The mechanism series (runaway, safeguards, the container, egregores) uses the same hand on a diagrammatically different subject — a vessel, a loop, a threshold.
hermetic: planetary glyph reduced to pure geometry
gestural: a single figure reduced to three strokes
an arrow that devours its own tail
structural: a vessel that holds a rising column
a membrane with a pinprick leak
a threshold with one foot over it
a stack that has begun to lean
a field of small marks obeying one drifting attractor

_negative_note_cross: `cross, crucifix, christian cross, religious symbol, crucifixion` were added after a MEASURED failure across the first square batch. SDXL's strongest attractor for 'occult emblem, ink on aged bone paper' is a CROSS: briefs naming a suitcase, a folding chair, a two-pan balance, a card drawer and an hourglass all came back as a crucifix. An emblem is not a devotional object, so a cross here is a WRONG STATEMENT about the post, not merely a stray. Measured with tools/headers/ab-neg.sh (append the clause, hold the positive prompt and seed fixed): 4 of the 5 plates returned the briefed object ('the-breakthrough' -> the folding chair, 'the-differential' -> a two-pan balance, 'set-and-setting' -> a threshold, 'the-designed-method' -> lost the cross). The positive prompt alone never governed this: the phrasing 'no border, no frame' and the whole negative list suppress text and ornament but name nothing that competes with a cross.
_style_note: ORDER: the gestural clause is FIRST and the subject text is assembled without medium vocabulary. Measured twice (tools/headers/ab.py, then again in the square era): a style clause buried mid-prompt loses to the subject text around it, so the hand must lead.
_object_anchor_note: MEASURED 2026-10-01: after the v5/v6 flip to gesture-primary, ~8 plates rendered as pure abstract ink masses with NO recognisable object (the-holy-hertics, the-lucifer-effect, the-machine-has-no-reading, the-differential, the-ladder-of-light, the-empty-vessel, the-follower, the-witch-and-the-debt). Diagnosed: (a) nothing in the style clause says the drawing DEPICTS anything, (b) the suffix said 'cropped by the frame edge', which crops the subject out, and (c) the negative banned 'emblem, seal, icon, stamp, medallion' — words that make a drawing READ — while trying to ban words that make it an ICON. Confirmed independently: a seed re-roll does NOT restore the object (4 rolls x these plates, none recovered), so this is a prompt defect, not a sampler basin. Fix: an explicit object anchor in compose() plus a no-crop suffix, with the icon-ness left to 'centred, symmetrical, mandala, radial symmetry, ornamental decoration'.
_token_budget_note: MEASURED 2026-10-01 AND IT EXPLAINS THE WHOLE SESSION'S FLAP: SDXL's text encoder takes 77 tokens per chunk and TWO chunks, so anything past ~154 tokens is SILENTLY DROPPED. The composed prompts averaged 303 tokens (max 364), i.e. more than double. The style clause sat in the first chunk and the SUBJECT, composition and accent were past the cut — so the model was rendering the hand and never read what to draw. Three consecutive single-variable A/Bs (negative sym words, engraving negatives, suffix diagonal) all came back TIES, which is the signature of editing text that is never seen. Every prompt is now assembled to a hard budget and the parts are dropped in priority order (composition first, then accent, then symbols) so the SUBJECT always survives inside the first chunk.
_legibility_note: MEASURED 2026-10-01 from USER PREFERENCE, and it reverses the direction of the v5/v6 flip: the user reviewed the batch and said they prefer the plates that LOOK LIKE SOMETHING over the abstract-gesture ones. Two independent vision QC passes agreed on a ~13-plate ABSTRACT set while ~46 read as recognisable objects, so legibility is already the majority and the job is to lift the minority, not to re-aim the whole style. What forced abstraction was a band of words in the style clause — 'asymmetric', 'spatter and drips', 'ragged unfinished edges trailing off', 'dry-brush texture', 'unfinished' — every one of which describes the MARK rather than the SUBJECT. They are removed here and replaced with explicit depiction language, while the ink/brush medium the user approved is kept. Note this ALSO retires the earlier over-correction: 'icons' were treated as a defect, but a recognisable depicted object is exactly what the user wants, so the anti-icon negatives now only guard the specific failure (ornamental mandala/symmetry).
